items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Isopropanol (C₃H₈O) — CID 3776. Secondary alcohol (rubbing alcohol) with a central CH-OH group.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: SN2 Mechanism: One-step concerted nucleophilic substitution with backside attack and Walden inversion of stereochemistry.

steps.title: Nucleophile Approach (Backside Attack)
steps.electronMovement: OH⁻ lone pair attacks the electrophilic carbon from 180° opposite to the leaving group (Br).
steps.explanation: Hydroxide ion attacks the partially positive C-α from backside, avoiding electron repulsion of bromide.

steps.title: Pentacoordinate Transition State
steps.electronMovement: Partial C-OH bond forms as partial C-Br bond weakens; central C assumes planar sp2 geometry.
steps.explanation: High energy trigonal bipyramidal transition state with partial negative charges on both entering and leaving groups.

steps.title: Leaving Group Departure & Inversion
steps.electronMovement: C-Br bonding pair departs onto Bromide (Br⁻); stereochemistry undergoes complete Walden Inversion.
steps.explanation: Bromide departs as a stable anion, completing umbrella-like inversion to produce Ethanol.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Electrophilic Addition of HBr to Ethene: Two-step addition across C=C double bond forming bromoethane.

metadata.title: Electrophilic Addition of HBr to Ethene

steps.title: Protonation of Double Bond
steps.electronMovement: π-electrons of C=C double bond attack H⁺ of HBr, breaking H-Br bond onto Br.
steps.explanation: Nucleophilic alkene π-cloud donates electron pair to electrophilic proton, forming an ethyl carbocation.

steps.title: Nucleophilic Attack by Bromide
steps.electronMovement: Bromide ion (:Br⁻) attacks carbocation carbon (C⁺) with lone pair.
steps.explanation: Nucleophilic bromide rapidly bonds to electron-deficient carbocation center to yield Bromoethane.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Acid-Catalyzed Hydration of Propene: Addition of water in presence of H₂SO₄ yielding Propan-2-ol.

steps.title: Electrophilic Proton Attack
steps.electronMovement: Alkene π-bond attacks H₃O⁺, protonating terminal carbon to generate 2° carbocation.
steps.explanation: Protonation occurs preferentially on terminal CH₂ according to Markovnikov rule to form stable 2° carbocation.

steps.title: Nucleophilic Addition of Water
steps.electronMovement: Oxygen lone pair on H₂O attacks 2° carbocation to form protonated alcohol oxonium ion.
steps.explanation: Water acts as nucleophile attacking electron deficient secondary carbocation.

steps.title: Deprotonation to Regenerate Acid
steps.electronMovement: Second H₂O molecule abstracts proton from oxonium ion, regenerating catalyst H₃O⁺.
steps.explanation: Deprotonation completes synthesis of Propan-2-ol while restoring acid catalyst.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: SN1 Mechanism: Two-step unimolecular substitution via planar carbocation intermediate producing racemic mixture.

steps.title: Rate-Determining Heterolysis
steps.electronMovement: C-Cl bond breaks heterolytically onto Chloride, generating tertiary carbocation.
steps.explanation: Slow rate-determining step producing stable planar tertiary carbocation intermediate.

steps.title: Frontside / Backside Nucleophilic Attack
steps.electronMovement: Nucleophile attacks planar C⁺ with equal probability from either face.
steps.explanation: Attack from top or bottom face yields racemic (50:50) product mix.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes in presence of peroxides yields Anti-Markovnikov product.

metadata.title: Anti-Markovnikov Addition of HBr (Peroxide / Kharasch Effect)
metadata.exceptionReason: Peroxide forms bromine free radicals (Br•). Br• attacks double bond first, generating the more stable 2° free radical, placing Br at less substituted carbon.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Applies ONLY to HBr (not HCl or HI) because both propagation steps are exothermic only for HBr.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Addition of HCl to 3-methyl-1-butene gives 2-chloro-2-methylbutane as major product.

metadata.title: Carbocation Rearrangement in Alkene Addition (1,2-Hydride Shift)
metadata.exceptionReason: Protonation forms initial 2° carbocation, which undergoes spontaneous 1,2-hydride shift to form hyperconjugated 3° carbocation before Cl⁻ attack.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Always check for hydride or methyl shifts whenever a 2° carbocation is adjacent to a 3° or 4° carbon.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Bromination of alkenes in CCl₄ proceeds strictly via Anti-addition (trans product).

metadata.title: Anti-Addition in Bromination (Halonium Ion Bridge)
metadata.exceptionReason: Formation of cyclic bromonium ion blocks frontside attack; second Br⁻ must attack from backside (180° opposite), giving anti stereochemistry.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Cyclic alkene halogenation yields trans-1,2-dibromide exclusively.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Oxymercuration-Demercuration gives Markovnikov alcohol without carbocation rearrangement.

metadata.title: Oxymercuration-Demercuration (Markovnikov without Rearrangement)
metadata.exceptionReason: Mercurinium ion intermediate prevents formation of free carbocation, avoiding 1,2-shifts while maintaining strict Markovnikov regioselectivity.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Use Hg(OAc)₂ / NaBH₄ when Markovnikov hydration is needed without skeletal rearrangement.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Hydroboration-Oxidation of alkenes with BH₃/THF followed by H₂O₂/OH⁻ gives Anti-Markovnikov syn-alcohol.

metadata.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation (Anti-Markovnikov Syn-Addition)
metadata.exceptionReason: Boron is less electronegative than Hydrogen; B adds to less hindered carbon while H adds to more hindered carbon in a concerted 4-center transition state.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Consistently yields Anti-Markovnikov alcohol with syn-stereochemistry.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Elimination of bulky alkyl halides with bulky base (t-BuOK) yields less substituted alkene (Hofmann product).

metadata.title: Hofmann Elimination Rule Exception (Saytzeff Violation)
metadata.exceptionReason: Bulky base cannot easily access acidic proton on internal carbon due to steric crowding; abstracts more accessible terminal proton instead.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Bulky bases (t-BuOK, LDA) produce less substituted alkenes as major products.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium gives 47% meta-nitroaniline.

metadata.title: Nitration of Aniline in Strongly Acidic Medium
metadata.exceptionReason: In concentrated H₂SO₄/HNO₃ mixture, aniline (-NH₂) is protonated to form anilinium ion (-NH₃⁺), which is strongly meta-directing and deactivating.
metadata.keyTakeaway: To get para-nitroaniline, acetylate -NH₂ first with acetic anhydride to protect it.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Reaction of Chlorobenzene with NaNH₂ in liquid NH₃ gives mixture of ortho and meta substituted anilines.

metadata.title: Nucleophilic Substitution on Aryl Halides via Benzyne Intermediate
metadata.exceptionReason: Strong base abstracts ortho-proton forming highly strained triple bond benzyne intermediate, followed by NH₂⁻ addition at either carbon.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Aryl halides without strong deactivating ortho/para groups react via elimination-addition (benzyne).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane yields isopropylbenzene (cumene) instead of n-propylbenzene.

metadata.title: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation Rearrangement to Cumene
metadata.exceptionReason: 1-chloropropane + AlCl₃ generates primary carbocation complex, which rearranges via 1,2-hydride shift to more stable 2° isopropyl carbocation.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Use Friedel-Crafts acylation followed by Clemmensen reduction to synthesize straight-chain alkylbenzenes.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Formaldehyde and Benzaldehyde undergo disproportionation under concentrated NaOH rather than Aldol condensation.

metadata.title: Cannizzaro Disproportionation (Non-Enolizable Aldehydes)
metadata.exceptionReason: Aldehydes lacking α-hydrogens cannot form enolate ions. Hydroxide attacks carbonyl carbon directly, triggering hydride transfer.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Yields equal moles of alcohol (reduced) and carboxylate salt (oxidized).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO₂ to yield Salicylic acid (ortho isomer) selectively over para isomer.

metadata.title: Ortho-Selectivity in Kolbe-Schmitt Reaction
metadata.exceptionReason: Sodium cation (Na⁺) forms a 6-membered chelate complex bridging oxygen and carbon dioxide, directing attack strictly to ortho position.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Potassium phenoxide (K⁺) gives para-hydroxybenzoic acid due to larger K⁺ ionic radius.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Substrates containing acid-sensitive acetal groups undergo decomposition during Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg/HCl).

metadata.title: Clemmensen vs Wolff-Kishner Reduction Compatibility
metadata.exceptionReason: Clemmensen requires conc. HCl (acidic), destroying acid-sensitive functional groups; Wolff-Kishner uses KOH/hydrazine (basic), destroying base-sensitive esters.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Choose Clemmensen for base-sensitive carbonyls and Wolff-Kishner for acid-sensitive carbonyls.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: R-Cl + NaI -> R-I + NaCl precipitate in dry acetone.

metadata.title: Finkelstein Halide Exchange Driven by Precipitation
metadata.exceptionReason: NaI is soluble in dry acetone, while NaCl and NaBr are insoluble and precipitate out, driving equilibrium forward via Le Chatelier's principle.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Solvent solubility difference drives an otherwise reversible substitution to 100% completion.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Reaction of tertiary alkyl halide with sodium methoxide yields 100% alkene (isobutylene), no ether.

metadata.title: Williamson Ether Synthesis Failure on 3° Halides
metadata.exceptionReason: Alkoxide ions (RO⁻) are strong bases as well as nucleophiles. With steric 3° halides, E2 elimination completely outcompetes SN2 substitution.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Always use 1° alkyl halide + 3° alkoxide for unsymmetrical tertiary ethers.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction brominates aliphatic carboxylic acids at α-position using Red Phosphorus and Br₂.

metadata.title: HVZ Selective Alpha-Bromination of Carboxylic Acids
metadata.exceptionReason: Red P + Br₂ generates acyl bromide intermediate (PBr₃ + RCH₂COOH -> RCH₂COBr), which enolizes readily for α-bromination before hydrolyzing back.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Requires at least one α-hydrogen; formic acid (HCOOH) and benzoic acid fail HVZ.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl₂) gives immediate turbidity with 3° alcohols, 5 min with 2°, none at RT with 1°.

metadata.title: Lucas Test Turbidity Differential via SN1 Carbocation
metadata.exceptionReason: Reaction proceeds via SN1 carbocation intermediate. 3° carbocation forms instantaneously; 1° carbocation is unstable and requires heating.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Insoluble alkyl chloride precipitation creates visual cloudiness (turbidity).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Ozonolysis of alkenes with Zn/H₂O stops at aldehydes; with H₂O₂ yields carboxylic acids.

metadata.title: Ozonolysis Workup Divergence (Zinc vs Peroxide)
metadata.exceptionReason: Zinc dust acts as a reducing agent to destroy hydrogen peroxide byproduct (H₂O₂), preventing aldehyde oxidation to carboxylic acid.
metadata.keyTakeaway: Use Zn/H₂O or (CH₃)₂S for aldehydes; use H₂O₂ for carboxylic acids.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Grignard reagents (RMgX) decompose instantly in water or ethanol to produce alkanes.

metadata.title: Grignard Reagent Destruction by Protic Traces
metadata.exceptionReason: RMgX is a super-strong base (pK_a ~ 50). Carbanion R⁻ abstracts acidic proton from H₂O or ROH exponentially faster than attacking carbonyls.
metadata.keyTakeaway: All Grignard reactions must be conducted in strictly anhydrous dry ether.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Phenol + CHCl₃ + KOH -> Salicylaldehyde (ortho-formyl phenol) via dichlorocarbene intermediate.

metadata.title: Dichlorocarbene Intermediate in Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
metadata.exceptionReason: CHCl₃ + KOH undergoes α-elimination forming neutral electrophilic dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂), which attacks phenoxide ion at ortho position.
metadata.keyTakeaway: If CCl₄ is used instead of CHCl₃, Salicylic acid is obtained.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Treatment of 2,3-dimethylbutene-2,3-diol (pinacol) with conc. H₂SO₄ yields t-butyl methyl ketone (pinacolone).

metadata.title: Pinacol-Pinacolone Rearrangement via Methyl Migration
metadata.exceptionReason: Protonation and loss of water forms 3° carbocation, followed by 1,2-methyl shift driven by oxonium ion resonance stabilization.
metadata.keyTakeaway: 1,2-diol rearranges to ketone upon acid treatment.
